CUDA (originally an acronym for Compute Unified Device Architecture) is a proprietary parallel computing platform and application programming interface (API) developed by Nvidia that allows software to use certain types of graphics processing units (GPUs) for accelerated general-purpose processing, significantly broadening their utility in artificial intelligence, scientific and high-performance computing. CUDA was created in 2004 and was officially released in 2007. 
CUDA is both a software layer that manages data, giving direct access to the GPU and CPU as necessary, and a library of APIs that enable parallel computation. In addition to drivers and runtime kernels, the CUDA platform includes compilers, libraries and developer tools to help programmers.
CUDA is written in the C programming language, but is designed to work with other programming languages including C++, Fortran, Python
